players.product: retail colocation & interconnection (IBX data centers, Equinix Fabric) and xScale hyperscale data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 headline results (normalized, constant currency), per CFO Olivier Leonetti: 'Recurring revenues were $2.3 billion, up 10% year-over-year'; 'Total revenues were $2.4 billion, up 8% year-over-year'; 'Adjusted EBITDA was $1.2 billion, up 13% year-over-year, resulting in a 51% Adjusted EBITDA margin'; quarterly AFFO surpassed $1 billion for the first time and AFFO per share was $10.79, up 10%. CEO: second straight quarter of double-digit MRR growth. Q1 results exclude the xScale Hampton lease, which slipped into Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: recurring revenues $2.3 billion (+10%); total revenues $2.4 billion (+8%); adjusted EBITDA $1.2 billion (+13%), 51% margin; AFFO per share $10.79

quarterly_data.signal: Record sales activity and backlog: CEO Adaire Fox-Martin said Q1 'was also the largest quarter of total sales activity in our history'; annualized growth bookings of $378 million, up 9% year-over-year, 'with approximately $140 million of pre-selling activity on top of that', i.e. 35% growth in total sales activity, 'resulting in a record backlog'. Over 3,800 transactions across more than 3,100 unique customers; the backlog of cabinets sold but not yet installed is at a record level. Pricing 'remains firm' for pre-sales and in-quarter bookings; no customer pullback from rising costs.
quarterly_data.figure: annualized growth bookings $378 million (+9%); approximately $140 million pre-selling; total sales activity +35%; over 3,800 transactions, more than 3,100 unique customers

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 guidance (point-in-time, before the Q2 raise): full-year total revenue guidance raised by $21 million to 10%-11% growth; adjusted EBITDA raised by $24 million to approximately 51% margin; AFFO raised by approximately $40 million to 10%-12% growth; AFFO per share growth 9%-11%; Q2 MRR growth of 10%-11%. Excluding xScale and land, total capex now expected at the top end of the prior range at $4.1 billion ($280 million-$300 million recurring, approximately $3.8 billion non-recurring), and the team 'continues to evaluate opportunities to accelerate our capacity'. Churn tracking toward the low end of the 2%-2.5% range per the CFO (CEO later said holding the 2-2.5 range).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue growth 10%-11% (raised by $21 million); AFFO growth 10%-12%; AFFO per share growth 9%-11%; 2026 capex $4.1 billion excl. xScale and land ($280 million-$300 million recurring, approximately $3.8 billion non-recurring)

quarterly_data.signal: AI inference ecosystem traction: 'eight of the top 10 AI model providers and four of the top five Neo-clouds are actively expanding with Equinix. They have placed more than 110 separate network nodes with us' - in addition to hyperscaler nodes. 'Approximately 60% of our largest deals in Q1 were AI-related' and 'large capacity Equinix Fabric connections have tripled from just a year ago'. CEO sees neoclouds shifting from training footprints to inference and enterprise customers, making them 'potential inference magnets' for the ecosystem (network nodes to CSPs/NSPs, AI inference nodes in dense metros, Fabric access to enterprises).
quarterly_data.figure: eight of the top 10 AI model providers and four of the top five Neo-clouds expanding; more than 110 separate network nodes; approximately 60% of largest deals AI-related

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnection and operating metrics: net interconnections +5,800 'with particular strength in Fabric additions'; 4,100 net cabinet billing; churn 1.7%, below the low end of the range (CFO: 'primarily due to the benefit of some delayed churn' and renewal execution; CEO cited 'the timing of some churn, including our Equinix Metal business' plus the renewal focus); MRR per cabinet $2,524, up 7%, 'reflecting the firm pricing environment and continued increase in density'. Interconnection revenue up 9%, Fabric revenue up 26%; Fabric bookings were cited as up 70% in prepared remarks and 74% in Q&A. More than 500,000 live interconnections. Portal orders 20,000, up 12%.
quarterly_data.figure: net interconnections 5,800; net cabinet billing 4,100; churn 1.7%; MRR per cabinet $2,524 (+7%); interconnection revenue +9%; Fabric revenue +26%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build: '46 major projects underway across 32 markets, including six xScale projects'; more than 70% of retail expansion capex in major metros, the rest mainly in Asia expansion markets; 'approximately 25% of our 2026 retail capacity expansion has already been sold' via pre-sales. Six projects opened since the last call across six metros. Q1 capex about $1.3 billion, approximately 90% growth/expansion. CEO: '3 GW currently either in land under control or in development'. Higher-density future facilities are still underwritten at mid-twenties% returns (SVP Finance Phillip Konieczny).
quarterly_data.figure: 46 major projects across 32 markets (six xScale); approximately 25% of 2026 retail capacity pre-sold; 3 GW land under control or in development; Q1 capex about $1.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Nordic expansion: Equinix 'signed a joint agreement with Canada Pension Plan Investment Board to purchase' atNorth (spelled 'atnNorth' in the transcript), giving access to 'an installed and active development pipeline of approximately 800 MW expected to come online over the next five years', including Copenhagen; subject to closing conditions and expected to be immediately accretive to AFFO per share.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 800 MW development pipeline over the next five years

quarterly_data.signal: xScale Hampton lease timing: CEO said Equinix is 'nearing execution on expanded mutual beneficial terms with our customer'. CFO: Q4 2025 guidance had assumed $54 million of non-recurring revenue from the deal; Q1 2026 guidance included expanded terms worth approximately $80 million of revenue, $65 million of AFFO and $0.65 of AFFO per share, now shifted into Q2 guidance with no full-year impact. Remaining 2026 xScale deals are 'relatively small in nature'; Minooka is 'something that we are still working on'; guide assumes total NRR of approximately 5.8% for the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Hampton expanded terms approximately $80 million revenue, $65 million AFFO, $0.65 AFFO per share shifted from Q1 to Q2; NRR approximately 5.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid cooling demand: CEO said Q1 was 'quite a significant quarter' for liquid cooling orders; 'Today, we have 36 deployments across our footprint of customers using liquid cooling', active across all regions - 'seven orders within Q1 across all of our regions, up 50% Q on Q'. Example: Maersk selected Equinix as its primary data center partner, including 'its first liquid-cooled AI deployment in Frankfurt'.
quarterly_data.figure: 36 deployments using liquid cooling; seven orders within Q1, up 50% Q on Q

quarterly_data.signal: Power is the binding constraint and energy cost is hedged: CEO said 'the availability of power would be the largest constraint in our environment'; as densification rises Equinix often must put space on hold at an IBX to protect other customers' service levels. CFO: 'Globally, we are more than 90% hedged for 2026', so minimal impact expected even if energy prices stay elevated after Middle East developments. Middle East footprint: 6 data centers, about 1% of total revenues; the DX3 Dubai construction project was impacted by the conflict.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 90% hedged for 2026; Middle East 6 data centers, about 1% of total revenues

quarterly_data.signal: Returns and balance sheet: after the annual refresh, '192 stabilized assets increased recurring revenue by 6% year-over-year, are collectively 82% utilized, and generated a 26% cash-on-cash return'; interconnection within that pool grows 9%. About $3.1 billion of cash and short-term investments; net leverage 3.8x; issued $1.5 billion of senior notes at a blended 3.1%. New CFO (previously CFO of Eaton and Johnson Controls) said debt will be the primary funding source, equity opportunistic, and 'The mid 25% is a target. That's not an aspiration' (return target on new capex; prepared remarks said mid-20% unlevered cash-on-cash returns) in 'a market where demand is over supply'.
quarterly_data.figure: 192 stabilized assets, 82% utilized, 26% cash-on-cash return; $3.1 billion cash; net leverage 3.8x; $1.5 billion senior notes at 3.1%

quarterly_data.signal: New AI products: the Equinix Distributed AI Hub, 'which we introduced at NVIDIA GTC', gives enterprises 'a single, private, low-latency connection to the entire AI ecosystem' and is positioned as neutral (access to all models and clouds); Equinix Fabric Intelligence, built into the Fabric interconnection platform, monitors network performance and adjusts configurations automatically, and is in preview with a number of customers and partners.
